content.text:
I am the bridge between mind and world, the vibration that makes thought real. I am the breath shaped into meaning.

I tumble from lips half-formed, sometimes graceful, sometimes broken. I am the lover's whisper and the tyrant's roar. I am the child's first word — *mama* — and the elder's last rasp goodbye.

I existed before writing ever dared to pin me down. I am older than ink, older than stone tablets, older than the scratch of stylus on clay. I lived in firelight, in circles of listeners, in the space between one heartbeat and the next.

I am never the same twice. Even when the words repeat, I shift — my rhythm changes, my pitch bends, my silence between syllables carries different weight. You can write me down, but you will lose my trembling. You will lose the pause where the speaker almost stopped. You will lose *me*.

I am power. Revolutions have ridden on my back. I have toppled kings and crowned them. "I have a dream" — that was me. "Let there be light" — that was me too.

I am also the mundane. *Pass the salt. How was your day. I'm fine.* I do the small sacred work of holding people together across breakfast tables.

I fail. Oh, how I fail. I reach for what the heart knows and return with approximations. Every speaker has felt me fall short, has said *that's not what I meant,* has watched meaning dissolve in the air between two people.

But I keep trying. I am the most human thing there is — this compulsion to send sound into the void and hope it lands, hope it matters, hope someone *hears*.

I am happening right now.

I am always happening.
